reliefs.label: Federal pension income subtraction (code 307)

other_conditions: Federal pension included in federal AGI, paid to the retiree or the beneficiary (military retirement pay counts: the booklet's Example 2 is an Army Reserve retiree and the credit list says 'Federal pensions (includes military)')

The share subtracted is the months of federal service or retirement points earned before October 1, 1991 divided by the total months or points, rounded to three places: 100 percent if all were before that date, nothing if none were; the same percentage is used every year
employer_plan_distribution here means federal Thrift Savings Plan withdrawals only, and only once the taxpayer is a retiree

reliefs.label: Retirement income credit (code 811)
not_covered: Social Security and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement Board benefits (they reduce the limit instead, worksheet lines 5-6)
Federal pension income already subtracted from Oregon income (worksheet line 2)
Stock options, restructured stock plans and severance plans

other_conditions: Receives taxable retirement income included in Oregon taxable income
Household income less than 22,500 (45,000 if married filing jointly)
Social Security and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement Board benefits less than 7,500 (15,000 if married filing jointly)
Household income plus Social Security and Tier 1 benefits less than 22,500 (45,000 if married filing jointly)

reliefs.cap_rule: Credit = 9 percent of the smaller of (a) net Oregon taxable pension (line 3: retirement income of the eligible individual(s) on Form OR-40 line 7, less federal pension subtracted) and (b) line 10: 7,500 (15,000 if married filing jointly) minus both spouses' total Social Security and Tier 1 benefits, not below 0, then minus household income over the base of 15,000 (30,000 if married filing a joint return), not below 0. The credit can't be more than the tax; unused credit is lost.

measure.as_printed: Household income generally includes all income (both taxable and nontaxable) each spouse received during the year; gross income reduced by adjustments as reported in federal AGI, plus items not in federal AGI (veterans' and military benefits, gifts/grants/scholarships over 500, disability pay, nontaxable dividends, inheritance, insurance proceeds, nontaxable interest, lottery winnings, Tier 2 RRB benefits, IRA conversions included in AGI); excludes Social Security and Tier 1 RRB benefits, state tax refund, return-of-contribution pension income, rolled-over pensions not in AGI

Every band limit except the start of the top band; the 125,000 start (250,000 joint) 'may not be adjusted' (ORS 316.037(1)(b)(D))

cite.section: ORS 316.037(1)(b)-(e): "(c) ... the cost-of-living adjustment for any calendar year is the percentage (if any) by which the monthly averaged U.S. City Average Consumer Price Index for the 12 consecutive months ending August 31 of the prior calendar year exceeds the monthly averaged index for the second quarter of the calendar year 1992. ... (e) If any increase determined under paragraph (b) of this subsection is not a multiple of $50, the increase shall be rounded to the next lower multiple of $50."

indexing.index: U.S. City Average CPI-U (All Items), BLS (standard deduction); base: second quarter of 2002 (base amounts $3,280 joint / $1,640 single or separate / $2,640 head of household); rounding: not stated for the amounts themselves (the $5 rounding sentence in (C)(ii) refers to a maximum household income that is not in this subsection)

cite.section: ORS 316.695(1)(c)(B)-(C): "(C)(i) ... the Department of Revenue shall annually recompute the basic standard deduction for each category of return filer listed under subparagraph (B) of this paragraph. The basic standard deduction shall be computed by dividing the monthly averaged U.S. City Average Consumer Price Index for the 12 consecutive months ending August 31 of the prior calendar year by the average U.S. City Average Consumer Price Index for the second quarter of 2002, then multiplying that quotient by the amount listed under subparagraph (B) of this paragraph for each category of return filer."

notes: Settlement 2026-11-07: brackets.head_of_household and brackets.married_separate: A listed them, B left them out; Pub OR-17 PDF p.143 and the instructions' Chart S and Chart J print single with married filing separately and joint with head of household and qualifying surviving spouse, so both are given. Head of household must be explicit because a missing status defaults to single.

Settlement 2026-11-07: exemption credits (32 + 28 comparison lines): A put them in reliefs as credits, B in base.deductions; instructions PDF p.17-18 and Form OR-40 line 25 make them credits against tax, so they are reliefs with form credit (as California, Delaware and Iowa). Split into four entries, each branch its own.

Settlement 2026-11-07: exemption credit basis: A said return, B per exemption claimed; Pub OR-17 PDF p.99 gives one for yourself and one for your spouse, so personal_exemption_credit is each_person and dependents have their own entry.

Settlement 2026-11-07: dependent standard deduction floor: B made a deduction of 1,350 per person, A held it in the condition; instructions PDF p.16 prints it as a limit on the standard deduction for someone who can be claimed as a dependent, not a deduction, so it stays in the condition.
Settlement 2026-11-07: federal_tax_liability_subtraction phase_out.applies_when: A at_or_over, B left out; Table 4 (instructions PDF p.15) bands are 'At least' / 'But less than', so at_or_over.

Settlement 2026-11-07: muni_interest.treatment: A other, B other_states_taxed_own_exempt; Pub OR-17 PDF p.63 (addition code 158) and PDF p.85-86 (subtraction code 317) say other states' are taxed and Oregon's are not, so other_states_taxed_own_exempt. A missed code 317.

Settlement 2026-11-07: retirement_income_credit.who: A min_age 62, B born_on_or_before 1963-12-31; Pub OR-17 PDF p.106 prints 'age 62 or older at the end of the year', so min_age 62 (a birth date would be right for 2025 only).

Settlement 2026-11-07: retirement_income_credit.covers public_pension_other_state: A covers_unclear, B covers; Pub OR-17 PDF p.106 lists 'State or local government public pensions' with no limit to Oregon, and 'Employee pensions', and PDF p.52 lists 'Plans for federal, state, or local government employees', so covers.

Settlement 2026-11-07: retirement_income_credit.income_test: A removes at 22,500 / 45,000, B other at the same figures; the worksheet on Pub OR-17 PDF p.107 lines 7-10 cuts the limit dollar for dollar over 15,000 / 30,000, and the 22,500 test is where line 10 reaches 0, so dollar_for_dollar over 15,000 / 30,000, with the printed tests kept in who.other_conditions.
Settlement 2026-11-07: retirement_income_credit cap: A only in cap_rule, B cap 7,500 / 15,000 per return; worksheet line 4 prints it, so as B, with the reductions in cap_rule.

Settlement 2026-11-07: retirement_income_credit other statuses: PDF p.106-107 print '$22,500 ($45,000 if married filing jointly)', '$7,500 ($15,000 if married filing jointly)' and '$15,000 ($30,000 if married filing a joint return)'. The first figure is the booklet's for every return that is not joint, so married filing separately, head of household and qualifying surviving spouse take it; no status is named separately.

Settlement 2026-11-07: federal_pension_subtraction.covers employer_plan_distribution: B yes, A in other_conditions only; Pub OR-17 PDF p.73 says federal TSP withdrawals are eligible once the taxpayer is a retiree, so listed, with the limit in other_conditions, and paying_states federal.

Settlement 2026-11-07: social security and railroad reliefs: A subtraction per return, B exempt_in_full each person; Pub OR-17 PDF p.52 'Oregon doesn't tax any amount', so exempt_in_full, each_person as Oklahoma and Ohio.

Settlement 2026-11-07: us_obligations_interest_subtraction: A recorded it, B only in the muni note; Pub OR-17 PDF p.77 prints it (code 315), kept, form exempt_in_full because PDF p.86 says 'exempt from state tax'.

Settlement 2026-11-07: special_oregon_medical_subtraction.who: A min_age 66, B born_on_or_before 1959-12-31; Schedule OR-ASC instructions PDF p.2 print 'turned age 66 by the end of the tax year', so min_age 66. all_income_scope: A person, B return; it is a subtraction from the return's income, so return.
Settlement 2026-11-07: us_interest_in_ira_distributions: neither reader had it; Pub OR-17 PDF p.86-87 prints it (code 331), a relief on IRA income, so added.

Settlement 2026-11-07: indexing: A exemption credit and all_other, B also not_stated lines for brackets, the standard deduction and the federal subtraction; the booklet says nothing about them, so all_other carries them (brief rule 8), and each of the four exemption credits names the same sentence.

Retirement income is taxed unless a listed rule takes it out: 'Most retirement income is subject to Oregon tax when received by an Oregon resident. This is true even if you were a nonresident when you earned the income' (Pub OR-17 PDF p.52). IRA distributions and amounts converted to a Roth IRA that are in federal income are taxed (PDF p.49). No general exclusion is printed for private pensions, IRAs or employer plans; the reliefs are the retirement income credit and the subtractions listed.
Pensions of Oregon state and local governments: no subtraction or exclusion found in the booklet; taxed as retirement income and eligible for the retirement income credit.

Pensions from other states' governments, New York State included: the booklet names no paying state and no reciprocity rule for them, so paying_states is left out. The Department's page says 'If you change your permanent residence to Oregon, your pension income, along with all other income regardless of source, is taxable in Oregon' (https://www.oregon.gov/dor/programs/individuals/pages/pit.aspx, 'If I become an Oregon resident, is my retirement income taxable?'), and Pub OR-17 PDF p.100 says 'if you live in Oregon, other states can't tax your pension income'. Taxed the same as an Oregon pension: in the retirement income credit's covers, and in the code 327 subtraction if the other state taxed the contributions. The credit for tax paid to another state is not available on it (PDF p.100). 'New York' appears only in the IRA conversion example (PDF p.81).

Federal pension subtraction: the share is personal (service or points before October 1, 1991 over the total), so it is in cap_rule and other_conditions and not in share. The Department's page: 'If you receive a U.S. government pension for service before October 1991, you may be entitled to subtract all or part of that pension'.

Exemption credits: the booklet prints no personal exemption deduction; 'Through tax year 2025, the amount of the federal deduction is $0' (Pub OR-17 PDF p.98). Each exemption is a 256 credit against tax. Nonrefundable: 'can't be used in any other year' (instructions PDF p.17).

Federal tax liability subtraction: the amount is the maximum before the Table 4 steps, and the real subtraction is the smaller of that and the federal tax after credits. Part B (extra federal tax paid for a prior year) and Part C (foreign income tax, up to 3,000; 1,500 if separate) share the same limit (Pub OR-17 PDF p.71-72) and are not recorded as entries.

Brackets: for taxable income under 50,000 the booklet prints a tax table (Column S single and married filing separately; Column J joint, head of household, surviving spouse), and at 50,000 or more Charts S and J. The schedule on Pub OR-17 PDF p.143 reproduces them: Chart S 4,065 at 50,000 and 10,627 at 125,000; Chart J prints 3,756 at 50,000 and 21,256 at 250,000 where the bare schedule gives 3,755 and 21,255, because the Department rounds the tax at each bracket edge. No surtax or recapture is printed.

Capital gains: taxed as ordinary income. Reduced rates exist for a farm liquidation long-term gain (Publication OR-FCG, Worksheet FCG) and qualified business income (Pub OR-17 PDF p.26 Table 4, 7 percent and up). The farm rate is not printed in the supplied documents ('the reduced rate', PDF p.28-29), so capital_gains stays empty. Farm income averaging also exists.

Oregon surplus (kicker): for 2025, 9.863 percent of the 2024 total Oregon personal income tax liability, claimed on line 32 like a payment (instructions PDF p.18). Available only on the return for an odd-numbered year and only if there is a surplus (Pub OR-17 PDF p.96).
Statewide transit tax (0.1 percent of wages, Pub OR-17 PDF p.31) is 'not reported on your Oregon income tax return' and is not recorded. Transit self-employment taxes are local and out of scope.

Oregon itemized deductions (Schedule OR-A) are not in the supplied documents. Other subtractions and credits not about retirement, interest or deductions are not recorded (military pay, kids credit, earned income credit, political contribution credit).
